clue.text: Commercial centre with mail being sent out

indicators.note: things sent out are scattered and dispatched, so the letters leave their order and are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business hub whose post is being dispatched to customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial centre' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Commercial'; 'centre' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile describes trade and merchants, so it is a direct synonym of commercial in the business sense.

clue.text: You must restrain little kid, not the first or last to give shout of excitement

indicators.note: losing the first and the last means both end letters of the word are dropped
to restrain is to hold something in, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you
a nipper is a little child; its outer letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A parent restraining a toddler who is shouting excitedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Nipper is British slang for a small child; 'You' is the archaic ye, which does the restraining.
explanation.definitionFit: Yippee is an exclamation people cry out when delighted or thrilled about something.

clue.text: Most worn-out stuff Eric's chucked

indicators.note: something chucked is thrown about carelessly, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eric throws away his shabbiest old belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruffy means shabby and untidy from wear, so the superlative is the most shabby or worn-out.

clue.text: Noble king who went mad, with head sinking down maximally

indicators.note: in a down entry the head is the top letter, and sinking as far as possible sends it to the very bottom

blocks.note: King Lear goes mad in Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A mad king slumped down as far as he can go.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of LEAR moves to the end, giving EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: Wrong piece of equipment for workshop

blocks.note: first meaning: wickedness or immoral conduct
second meaning: a clamp fixed to a bench to hold work steady

explanation.surface: Someone has picked the incorrect tool for the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' reads as an adjective, but here it is a noun, a sin; the British spelling of the clamp matches it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both moral wrongdoing and a bench-mounted gripping tool used by carpenters and metalworkers.

clue.text: To this point one is only an imaginary beast?

blocks.note: as yet means up to now
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sceptic insists that so far the creature remains a myth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that some believe the creature is real.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a legendary ape-like creature said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Drunk is captured in something of a pantomime act

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters stumble into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk is caught in the middle of a slapstick stage routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like a noun for a person being captured, but it is the anagram signal. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage comedy full of slapstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a pie of sweet sauce into a face is a classic slapstick gag in comic stage shows.

clue.text: Birds that are little, not grand, rising from stones

indicators.note: grand is abbreviated to a single letter, which is to be left out
in a down entry rising means reading from the bottom upward, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: eaglets are young, small eagles

explanation.surface: Fledglings flutter up from among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand comes out of EAGLETS, and EALETS read upwards gives STELAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stelae are upright carved stone slabs or pillars, used in antiquity as monuments or gravestones.

clue.text: Tramp sleeping rough maybe has collected one set of papers

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: a dosser is British slang for someone who sleeps rough
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A homeless man has picked up a bundle of documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents gathered together about one person or subject.

clue.text: Finally you may get left in space flying in this?

definitions.text: Finally you may get left in space flying in this?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the following word
flying suggests letters being sent through the air and landing in a different order

blocks.note: the end letter of you
L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronaut wonders if they might be stranded in orbit inside their craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a space capsule could indeed leave its passenger stuck in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule is the small crewed compartment of a spacecraft, in which astronauts travel through orbit.

clue.text: Learner will soon be leaving primary school to pay attention

blocks.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

blocks.clueFragment: will soon be leaving primary school
blocks.note: a child who is ten will move up from primary school at eleven

explanation.surface: A pupil about to move up to secondary school is told to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: British children leave primary school at eleven, so a child who IS TEN will soon be leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to give heed and concentrate on what is being said.

clue.text: Woman setting about some men nastily

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
to set something about is to turn it round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A woman lays into a group of men in a nasty way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting about' reads as attacking, but it signals turning letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a common female first name, and crosswords freely use a woman to clue one.

clue.text: Switch in plane trip to give source of illumination

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here within the word for a journey by air

blocks.note: a journey by aeroplane
a switch is a thin whip, and to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: A passenger flicks a switch on an aircraft to turn on a reading lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a light switch but means a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashlight is the American term for a battery-powered hand torch that gives out light.

clue.text: Superstar idol? Time to get into hard world, little fellow!

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it, so one letter enters the other piece

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the earth is our world
T is the abbreviation for time
Rob is a short form of the name Robert

explanation.surface: A star is told it is time to get into the tough real world, little man.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is a celebrity, usually an actor or singer, whom fans adore, so an idol; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Clothes receptacle that's green inside -- bit of headgear kept outside it

indicators.note: inside places one word within the receptacle word
something kept outside wraps round the whole of what has been built so far

blocks.note: a hat is an item of headwear
a bin is a container
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A green-lined wardrobe bin with a hat hanging on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Habiliment is an old or formal word for clothing, attire or dress.

clue.text: Home food, it's said, is natural

indicators.note: it's said tells us to take the sound of the word spoken rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
bread is a staple food

explanation.surface: Someone claims home cooking is the natural choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred qualities are innate, deeply ingrained from birth, which is natural in the sense of inborn.

clue.text: Young rebel once defeated prominent LibDem but not Conservative

indicators.note: but not means remove the following item from the name just given

blocks.note: to beat is to defeat
Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats and was deputy prime minister
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political report on a young upstart beating a senior Liberal Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The LibDems are Britain's Liberal Democrat party; Nick Clegg joined a coalition with the Conservatives, which makes 'but not Conservative' a sly joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatnik was a member of the 1950s Beat Generation, young bohemians rejecting convention, hence 'once'.

clue.text: City engineers in South Africa and Britain

indicators.note: in places one abbreviation inside the abbreviation that follows it

blocks.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
GB stands for Great Britain
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are working in two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital and largest city of Croatia.

clue.text: Splatter item of furniture with gold and black

blocks.note: a bed is a piece of furniture
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Someone splashes gold and black paint over a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or plaster something messily with paint or dirt.

clue.text: Ardent temp working in part of the firm

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over and processed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic temporary worker is busy in one section of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a division of a business handling one area, such as sales or accounts.

clue.text: Pieces for one not quite secure?

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: solid means firm and secure

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something meant for a single person is a little unsafe.
explanation.walkthrough: Soli is the Italian plural of solo, used for musical pieces played by one performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a piece performed by a single musician, and soli is one of its plurals.

clue.text: Good person with something irritating, a sort of pain

blocks.note: ST is short for saint, a good person
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A saintly person putting up with an irritating, painful nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sudden sharp pain in the side, often brought on by running.

clue.text: Hearing not good? It's awful -- a medical condition

indicators.note: good is abbreviated to a single letter, which is to be dropped
something awful is in a terrible mess, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the G for good is taken away

explanation.surface: A patient complains that poor hearing is a dreadful ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is a medical condition in which an organ pushes through the wall of muscle containing it.

clue.text: Ruler from East on edge after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the word for edge is read backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A deposed Eastern ruler on the brink after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising, which suits a ruler, but it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: Very loudly disposed of a strong drink

indicators.note: something disposed of is got rid of, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: stiff means strong, as in a stiff drink
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone noisily knocks back a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong drink' looks like one phrase, but 'a strong' is wordplay and 'drink' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Unbelief is conveyed in article by those people

indicators.note: something conveyed in is carried inside, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
them refers to those people
taken as written

explanation.surface: Disbelief is spread through a newspaper piece written by certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the absence of belief in any god, which is religious unbelief.

clue.text: Permit unknown character to show disapproval? Fine!

blocks.note: a ticket is a permit to enter or travel
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
to boo is to jeer disapprovingly

explanation.surface: A ticket-holder lets a stranger jeer, then gives a shrug of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned British slang meaning fine or in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jaunty colloquial way of saying everything is all right and going well.

clue.text: Stick designation of drug on container

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, so the drug's letter is sent second

blocks.note: a can is a tin container
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A label naming a drug is stuck onto its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B can mean A comes after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane is a walking stick, or a rod used for support or punishment.
